interest: Shows 1939-41 US restriction of Japanese tankers from Hawaiian ports, tightening into export licensing before the 1941 asset freeze.
overview: This file (File 181) consists of a nineteen-page Department of State 'List of Papers' (docket sheets 92 through 110) for decimal file 894.3311 ('Visits of Vessels and Aircraft of Japan to Ports of United States'), logging diplomatic and interdepartmental communications from December 1939 through August 1941 (sub-numbers 589/598 through 722). The docket registers formal requests submitted by the Japanese Embassy in Washington for Japanese naval transports, tankers, and training ships—including the Erimo, Iro, Shiriya, Kyokuto Maru, Kokuyo Maru, Hayatomo, Taisei Maru, and Toei Maru—to call at United States ports, predominantly Los Angeles, San Francisco, Honolulu, and Hilo, primarily to replenish water and provisions and to load crude petroleum and fuel oil. It tracks extensive interdepartmental coordination among the State Department, Navy Department, War Department, Treasury Department (Customs), Labor and Justice Departments (Immigration), Interior Department, and state and territorial authorities. Crucially, the entries illustrate the gradual tightening of American security restrictions prior to the Pacific War, including the exclusion of Japanese naval vessels from Hawaiian ports outside Honolulu following the Yakumo incident and sentry controversies at Hilo, the redirection of tankers away from Fleet concentrations at San Pedro to San Francisco, intelligence reporting on naval personnel aboard chartered tankers, and the institution of Treasury and State Department petroleum export licensing requirements in mid-1941.

subfiles.about: A docket list registering communications, diplomatic notes, and interdepartmental clearances regarding the visits of Japanese public and naval vessels to United States ports from December 1939 to August 1941.
subfiles.summary: This nineteen-page register (Sheets 92 through 110) records incoming and outgoing documents (sub-numbers 589/598 through 722) within State Department decimal file 894.3311. It logs official notifications and requests from the Japanese Embassy for naval transports and auxiliary vessels—including the Erimo, Iro, Shiriya, Kyokuto Maru, Kokuyo Maru, Taisei Maru, Hayatomo, and Toei Maru—to visit American ports such as Los Angeles, San Francisco, Honolulu, and Hilo to obtain fuel oil and provisions. The register tracks internal U.S. government coordination among the State, Navy, War, Treasury, Labor, and Justice Departments regarding clearance conditions, crew shore liberties, and cargo inspections. Significant entries record the exclusion of Japanese public vessels from Hawaiian ports outside Honolulu following the Yakumo incident, the redirection of tankers away from Fleet concentrations at San Pedro/Los Angeles, and the tightening of crude oil export licensing by the Treasury and State Departments in mid-1941.
